version.value: Original version for two violins, two violas and two cellos; one continuous work divided across two LP sides.
version.note: The break between bars 228 and 229 is an editorial score/audio inference: side 1 ends with the E♭-minor-to-B♭ link on score p. 25; side 2 begins with the D-major Sehr breit und langsam on p. 26. Not the 1917 or 1943 string-orchestra arrangement.

performers.note: The quartet’s four members are supplemented by Dinkin and Reher. The source does not identify a conductor; none is invented.

date.note: These are recording dates, independently distinguished from the 1950 release year and 2021 transfer.

place.note: The archive establishes the city, not a specific studio or room.

catalogue.note: The later P-8304 reissue is not the source carrier used here.

composition.value: The original sextet score was published in 1905; its early-publication public-domain basis in the United States is separate from rights in later editions or arrangements.
composition.note: This record contains instrumental music, not a sung or recited translation of Dehmel’s poem. No later editorial score or translation licence is asserted.

recording.value: EU territorial phonogram-term basis: first lawful publication in 1950, before 1963. US recording status not established.
recording.note: Programme rule 3; the Arnold Schönberg Center independently identifies the 1950 original issue. No Creative Commons licence is claimed for the Archive transfer.
